overall: The AG found the Somerset Zoning Board of Appeals did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of the three allegations arising from its October 12 meeting, and advised the complainant not to file repeat complaints on the counsel-referral issue.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair did not announce the meeting was being recorded, contending the word 'recorded' had to be used.
allegations.key_passage: This statement clearly informed attendees that the meeting was being recorded; any assertion to the contrary is not made in good faith.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board voted to authorize counsel to respond to seven prior Open Meeting Law complaints without a full review of them during a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: that a public body may have chosen to refer a complaint to legal counsel rather than discuss its substance is the public body's prerogative.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board referred to complaints by number rather than reading them aloud, which prevented the public from understanding their substance.
allegations.key_passage: We find no error in the manner in which the Board handled the complaints and note a public body may even choose to review Open Meeting Law complaints entirely in executive session.
